To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) slow and very slow desorption are observed for all soils and sedments and all compounds, and (2 ) the distribution over the three desorption fractions and the corresponding rate constants are independent of the sorbent and the sorbate.

slow and very slow desorption of chlorobenzen and PCBs from soils and sedments is (1) independent of the OC content of the soil/sediment, (2) independent of the polarity of the OM, (3) independent of the aromaticity of the OM, and (4) independent of the hydrophobicity of the compound.

slow and very slow desorption of PCB's and chlorobenzoates is a common phenomenon in soils and sediments, that the distribution over the rapidly desorbing, slowly desorbing, very slowly desorping, and non-desorbing fractions depends on sorbate hydrophobity, and that the rate constants for slow and very slow processes are not dependent on sorbent characteristics and are rather constant among the different sorbates and soils/sediments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetics of slow desorptions from soils and sediment.
the kinetics of slow desorbing fractions in a series of soils and sediments with widely different characteristics.
a new type of sorbent-controlled slow desorption, in which the slow desorption is not related to intra-OM diffusion but to the sorbate-sorbent interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

slow desorption is a process that involves a change in sorption mechanism from a sorbate-OM interaction to a sorbate-particle surface interaction, which is characterized by a low activation enthalpy of around 60 kJ/mol.
the slow and very slow desorption of chlorobenzen and PCBs from soil and sediment is not due to diffusion in the organic matter.
slow and very slow desorption of PCB and chlorobenene from soils and sedments are related to sorbate hydrophobity, but not to sorbent characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
slow and very slow desorption are related to the hydrophobic nature of the sorbed compounds, but not to the properties of the organic matter.
the rate of slow desorption of PCB and chlorobenzene congeners from soils and sedimens is controlled by sorbent and not sorbate characteristics.
sorbent characteristics (e.g. OC and OM content) do not determine slow desorption kinetics, but sorbate hydrophobity is a key factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate constants of the slow and very slow desorption of a wide range of hydrophobic compounds are rather constant among soils and sediments and among the compounds studied.
sorbent characteristics are not the determining factors for the kinetics of slow and very slow desorption.

the slow and very slow desorption of chlorobenzen and PCBs from soils and sedments can be described by a single rate constant, which is rather constant among sorbates and soils/sediments, and that sorbate hydrophybicity is an important parameter for this desorption.
